sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Finding the quote on the page
sections.what: Gathers the page's visible text, normalises it, and looks for the quote. Only the first visible match counts, since pages often hide copies of the same text in menus or print blocks. Marks the first match to show where it is.
sections.why: The header comment says matching must ignore case, spacing, punctuation and quote-style differences so that a quote split by tags or line breaks is still found.
sections.watch_out: Visibility is judged from the size and style of the text, so a page that hides text in unusual ways could still be matched.

sections.name: File setup: for
sections.title: Highlighting, closest match, banner and scroll helpers
sections.what: Wraps every part of the matched text in a highlight mark, using colours for the main match, a partial match or an anchor. Scrolls the first highlight into the centre of the view. Also holds the helper that finds the closest partial phrase, the helper that draws the top banner, and the helper that scrolls the whole page to load lazy content.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The highlight colours and banner suggest the output is a screenshot meant for human review.
sections.watch_out: Text that cannot be wrapped, for example across some element boundaries, is skipped silently, so a highlight can be partial. The scroll helper stops at 20,000 pixels.

sections.name: call
sections.title: Building the call to run a script
sections.what: Builds the text that asks the browser to run one of these functions, passing an argument if one is given.
sections.why: Likely reason: the browser needs a single expression to run, so the argument is packed into the call text.
sections.watch_out: The argument is turned into JSON text, so anything that cannot be converted to JSON will not work as an argument.

summary: Holds small pieces of JavaScript, stored as text, that the capture service runs inside a web page to find, highlight, scroll to and label a quote.
purpose: Lets the capture service check a live web page for a quote and produce a screenshot that shows it, without the server needing to read the page's structure itself.
why: The header comment says the scripts are kept as text so they run in the browser exactly as written, untouched by the server's TypeScript build. The file also says it was ported from a reference script.
how: First, the page's visible text is gathered and normalised so punctuation and case do not matter. Then the quote is located, its text is wrapped in coloured highlight marks, and the page is scrolled to it. A separate helper finds the longest matching part of the quote when the full quote is missing. Other helpers draw a banner across the page and scroll the page to load content. A last helper builds the call text that runs one of these functions with an argument.
inputs: The quote text to search for, a highlight mode (primary, partial or anchor), a label for the banner, and the page itself when the scripts run.
outputs: A true or false result for whether the quote was found and highlighted, the longest matching phrase when no full match exists, and visible changes to the page such as highlights, banners and scrolling.
risks: Matching ignores punctuation and spacing, so an unrelated run of words could match. Changes here must stay in step with the server-side normalisation in captureService. The scripts run inside pages that may be hostile or broken.
debug: If quotes are missed, first compare the normalisation rules here with those in captureService. If highlights are missing, check the visibility test and whether the wrapping step skipped segments. If scrolling is wrong, check the height limit in the scroll helper.
